summary: David Higgins specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held researcher posts at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, where he is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

David J. Kalupahana studied at the University of Ceylon and earned his PhD at the University of London under Stanley Weinstein and David Friedman. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, he served at Ceylon and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

David John McCutchion studied at Jesus College, Cambridge. Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, he taught literature at Visva-Bharati University (1957), was Reader in Comparative Literature at Jadavpur University (~1960–1972), and visited the University of Sussex (~1967–1968).

David Jones earned his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, working in philosophy and religious studies. Attested in 2007, he served as professor at the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies.

David K. Wyatt, a historian, studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell. He held posts at SOAS (~1963–1968) and the University of Michigan (~1968–1969) before chairing the Department of History at Cornell University (1969–2002).

David Kerman Tomlinson works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold, having also studied under Jay L. Garfield and Andy Rotman, and held a post at Smith College.

David Kopf studied at the University of Chicago (~1960–1964). Working in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology, he held a post at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities from ~1967 to 1997.
David L. Gosling specializes in religious studies and Indology. He held a Spalding Fellowship at Clare Hall, University of Cambridge in 1992 and was attested at the University of Cambridge in 2001.

David L. Haberman, a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at the University of Colorado Boulder. He held posts at the University of Arizona and Indiana University Bloomington, where he was attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

David L. McMahan works in Buddhist and religious studies. After teaching at the University of California, Santa Barbara and the University of Vermont, he served at Franklin & Marshall College as Assistant Professor (attested 2002) and Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2013).

David Llewellyn Snellgrove studied at Cambridge and Southampton, training under H. W. Bailey, D. R. Shackleton Bailey, Walter Simon, and Giuseppe Tucci. A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he was a professor at SOAS, University of London (1950–1982).

David Lopes studied at the Curso Superior de Letras and INALCO. Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he taught at the Liceu Central (1895), Curso Superior de Letras (1901), and the University of Lisbon (~1913–1937).

David Ludden studied at Yale and the University of Pennsylvania. Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he held posts at the University of Virginia (1979–1980), the University of Pennsylvania (1981–2008), and New York University (attested 2007).

David M. DiValerio studied at Wesleyan and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer. A scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, he joined the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee faculty in 2011.

David M. Knipe studied under Mircea Eliade (~1965–1971) and worked in Indology and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–2002), where he served as Professor of South Asian Studies and later Professor Emeritus.

David Magier works in Indology and linguistics. He served as Head of Area Studies at Columbia University (attested 1991–1996) and held positions at Princeton University Library, including Associate University Librarian for Collections & Access Services (attested 2024).

David Matsumoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004, 2013) and as President Emeritus at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

David Max Moerman specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held a post at Barnard College (attested 2007–2008) and is attested in 2026 as Professor and Department Chair at Barnard College, Columbia University.
David Mellins specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held posts at Columbia University (attested 2002–2005) and Rutgers University (attested 2006).

David Mitchell, a scholar in linguistics and Indology, completed undergraduate studies at Cleveland State University and a master's at Ohio State University (2009–2019). He was appointed Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2015.
